newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Coinbra opens new soy plant in Sao Paulo.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Coinbra opens new soy plant in Sao Paulo.

text.p: Brazilian food processor Coinbra, a division of Louis Dreyfus, has opened a soybean crushing and refining plant in Sao Paulo state in order to cater increasingly for domestic demand, a company official said.
Coinbra is renting the plant, owned by Comove, for 850,000 reais per year with an option to buy once Comove's bankruptcy proceedings are over, the official said.

"It is a strong possibility (that we will buy the facility). It's a question of price," he said. Coinbra, which has no crushing facilities in the region, wanted to test the local market before making a commitment, he added.
The plant, in Orlandia, has a daily crushing capacity of 1,200 tonnes of soybeans and a refining capacity of 300 tonnes soyoil per day, the official said.
"It is currently operating at half capacity. There are two plants with a capacity of 600 tonnes each," he said.
"We will shortly be using the second one in order to test it and see what maintenance work needs to be done, but we don't expect it to be fully operational until next year," he added.
Coinbra plans to invest a total $2.0 million in a maintenance overhaul of the Oberlandia facility, which has lain idle for four years. It has already spent around half that amount, the official said.

"With this plant, it will be possible to attend both (domestic and export) markets," he said. "At the beginning, as we are only just entering the region now...it is possible that we will have to export some of our product."

Coinbra currently owns seven crushing plants with a total capacity of 6,000 tonnes per day, in addition to the 1,200 tonnes of the new plant. Its oil refining capacity is of 600 tonnes per day, including the Orlandia plant.
The company expects to process more than two million tonnes of soybeans in 1997 worth around 650 million reais, the official said.
